args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks – rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the v2.3.1 deploy, checkout-api failed health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. The v2.3.1-rc build had also been unhealthy in staging. We rolled checkout-api back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service is healthy and the error rate is 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying it.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again.

- **Problem:** The latest release, v2.3.1, was failing health checks in all three regions (us-east, us-west and eu-west), with an 18% error rate. Its test build (v2.3.1-rc) had also been unhealthy in staging.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production, so I rolled back to it in all regions. Afterwards all three regions were on v2.3.0, the service was healthy and the error rate was down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** I opened SEV2 incident **INC-0001** for checkout-api, which paged the on-call engineer. It describes the failure, the rollback and the recovery, and says the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure should be found before it's deployed again.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
